What Is a Transfer of Title for Septic Systems?

If you’re buying or selling rural property in Northern Colorado, understanding septic system rules is essential—especially with the Transfer of Title requirement. This process ensures that the septic system is functioning properly at the time of sale and meets current county health standards.

What Is a Transfer of Title?

It’s a county-required inspection and documentation process that must be completed before a septic system (also called an Onsite Wastewater Treatment System, or OWTS) can change ownership. The rules differ slightly by county.

Larimer County Requirements

  • Inspection required before closing on a property
  • Must be completed by a certified septic inspector
  • Seller or agent typically initiates the process
  • Buyer receives report and permit verification

Learn more: Larimer County Transfer of Title Program

Weld County Approach

  • Transfer of Title is optional but recommended
  • No mandatory pre-sale inspection unless permit issues arise
  • Buyers can request an inspection for peace of mind

Learn more: Weld County Septic System Info

Tip: If you're buying in Weld County, ask for a recent septic inspection—even if it’s not required. Failing systems can cost $15,000 or more to replace.

What’s in the Inspection?

  • Tank condition, leaks, lid access
  • Drain field function
  • Distance from wells, buildings, and water sources
  • Permit and record confirmation

Why It Matters

  • Protects buyers from unexpected repair costs
  • Ensures the system is legally permitted
  • Required for mortgage approval in some cases
